idiom_name: ZIO service pattern: trait + Live class + ZLayer constructor
implementation_notes: In the Scala effect ecosystem the service layer is built from three pieces: a trait holding the operations, a final class holding its dependencies as constructor parameters (the Live implementation), and a ZLayer that lifts that constructor into the dependency graph - the effect type carries the service requirement, and the layer is assembled once at the edge with provide/layer composition so the transaction or transactor resource is scoped to a layer rather than an annotation. The structure is not replaced, only its wiring: the container becomes the type system plus ZLayer, and construction is effectful and resource-aware. A plain Scala service with explicit construction remains the right choice when the graph is small.
pitfalls: A ZLayer is a recipe, not a value: rebuilding layers per request or per test re-creates pools and transactors instead of sharing them.
ZLayer.fromZIO on a resourceful effect lets the resource outlive construction - use ZLayer.scoped for anything that must be released.
Large environment types produce unreadable compile errors; keep the service graph honest instead of dumping everything into one layer.
